hero.lead: The world’s largest cocoa producer, 32.7 million strong, which swapped expensive debt to free about EUR 330 million for its schools.

stats.label: Freed for schools by a debt swap

capital.heading: Côte d’Ivoire pioneers new instruments. Next, every child reading by ten.

record.text: Debt-for-development swap: Guarantee behind a cheaper loan; about EUR 330 million freed for education over five years
Extended Fund Facility, Extended Credit Facility and RSF: $3.5 billion EFF/ECF and $1.3 billion RSF; about $833 million released in June 2026
Health, nutrition and early childhood: Services for millions of mothers and children
Community and local development in the West (COSO West): About 1.8 million people
Public debt, share of GDP, 2025: down from 59.5% in 2024, the first fall in more than a decade

register.name: Treasury bonds by auction, with the first 20-year bond in the Union
register.detail: Auction 6 October 2026 · 364-day bills and 3-, 5-, 7- and 20-year bonds · 20-year bond at 6.25%, due 7 October 2046
register.note: FCFA 88 billion raised against FCFA 80 billion offered, with bids of about FCFA 128 billion
register.text: Côte d’Ivoire sold Treasury bills and bonds on the WAEMU regional market through UMOA-Titres, including FCFA 25 billion offered in a 20-year bond. No issuer in the Union had borrowed for so long on the regional market before, financial news reports say. Longer debt in the nation’s own currency spreads repayments over two decades.

register.name: Eurobond, 15 years
register.detail: Priced 18 February 2026 · 15 years · 5.39% in euros after currency hedging
register.note: Order book of $6.3 billion from about 270 investors
register.text: About FCFA 725 billion raised on international markets, all of it for the 2026 budget, with the aim of optimising the debt amortisation profile, the Ministry of Economy said.
by: Ministry of Economy, Finance and Budget of Côte d’Ivoire

register.name: Public bond offering 2025 on the regional market
register.note: More than FCFA 450 billion, above the FCFA 400 billion target
register.text: Two new bonds of five and seven years, also offered in exchange for maturing bonds, sold on the WAEMU regional market.
by: Ministry of Economy, Finance and Budget of Côte d’Ivoire

register.name: Regional gas market project (PRIME-GAS)
register.detail: Approved 29 June 2026 · IDA · With Benin and Togo
register.text: Prepares a regional gas market: coordinated gas imports, national gas master plans, harmonised rules and infrastructure ready for private finance, which the World Bank expects to unlock about $1.5 billion of private investment and lower energy costs.

register.name: Private Investment and Productive Jobs, first development policy financing
register.detail: Approved 5 June 2026 · Budget support · IDA and IBRD
register.text: Budget support for reforms that bring more private investment into energy, digital services, water, agribusiness and health, and that ease land rights, investment rules, tax design and the match between skills and jobs. It is aimed at productive jobs, the base of the livelihood standard.

register.name: Community and local development in the West (COSO West)
register.detail: Approved 19 May 2026 · IDA · 35 sub-prefectures of Tonkpi, Guémon and Cavally
register.text: Channels IDA resources to the Western Montagnes District for health centres, schools, clean water systems, and storage and processing facilities. Livelihood grants help about 46,000 people, mostly young people and women, start income-generating activities. It serves several of the seven standards at once.

register.name: Health, nutrition and early childhood
register.detail: Approved 30 April 2026 · $200M IDA credit and $25M GFF grants · Second phase of a multiphase programme
register.note: Services for millions of mothers and children
register.text: Supports universal health insurance with trained health workers, essential medical supplies and equipped facilities, a national digital health platform and performance-based financing for primary health facilities. It plans nutrition services for nearly one million children under five and early childhood services for more than 730,000 children.
by: Global Financing Facility for Women, Children and Adolescents

register.name: Debt-for-development swap
register.note: Guarantee behind a cheaper loan; about EUR 330 million freed for education over five years
register.text: A buy-back of the most expensive commercial debt, refinanced with a cheaper, longer loan and spent on schools.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility, Extended Credit Facility and RSF
register.note: $3.5 billion EFF/ECF and $1.3 billion RSF; about $833 million released in June 2026
register.text: The fiscal deficit fell to the regional ceiling of 3 percent of GDP in 2025.

register.name: Climate resilience and forest restoration in the Niger Basin (PIDACC-BN)
register.detail: Launched 16 September 2026, Bouaké · African Development Fund loan, Forest Investment Programme loans and grant, Government contribution
register.note: About 30,000 people, many of them women and young people
register.text: Restores forest cover in the former cocoa belt through seedlings, agroforestry and plantation restoration, and supports livestock, market gardening and agro-processing in five central regions. It links standing forest to farm incomes, the livelihood standard.

register.name: Yabayo–Buyo road, with boreholes and school and health centre works
register.detail: Ratified by the Council of Ministers 22 July 2026 · 60 km road and 8 km of urban roads
register.note: Includes ten drinking water boreholes in Buyo
register.text: Part-finances the paving of the 60 km Yabayo–Buyo road in the south-west, with town roads, fencing for schools and health centres, public spaces and ten drinking water boreholes. The road is meant to help farmers move their produce to market, serving the livelihood and water standards.

register.name: A larger stake in Shelter Afrique Development Bank
register.detail: Ratified by the Council of Ministers 22 July 2026 · Stake raised from 4% to 10%
register.text: BADEA finances Côte d’Ivoire’s larger shareholding in Shelter Afrique Development Bank (ShafDB), a bank dedicated to social housing and urban development. A larger stake gives the nation more weight in a lender for the shelter standard.
by: Arab Bank for Economic Development in Africa (BADEA)

register.name: Electricity access and grid strengthening, second phase (PROSER II)
register.detail: Approved 15 May 2026 · Total cost EUR 234.56 million, with EUR 83.96 million from the IsDB and EUR 47.46 million from the Government
register.note: More than 107,000 households to be connected; 244 rural localities electrified
register.text: Electrifies 244 rural localities across 18 regions and extends and strengthens distribution networks in Greater Abidjan, the interior and 12 departmental capitals, with 74,010 LED street lights. It serves the energy standard directly, home by home.

register.name: Anchor investment in the Electricity for All (PEPT 2) social bond
register.detail: Approved 15 October 2025 · Up to XOF 15 billion of an XOF 60 billion social bond · Tranches of 7, 10 and 15 years
register.note: 400,000 new connections over 2025–2026, benefiting 2.2 million people
register.text: The African Development Bank anchors the first local-currency social bond of the Electricity for All programme, a securitisation managed by ALC Titrisation, with up to EUR 6.9 million more from the Sustainable Energy Fund for Africa. It finances household connections to the grid, 35 percent of them for rural communities.

register.name: Bouaké and Yopougon markets, complementary financing
register.detail: Ratified by the Council of Ministers 22 July 2026
register.text: Complementary AFD financing for the development of the Bouaké and Yopougon markets. Markets are where traders earn their living, so the line serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Sustainability-linked sovereign loan
register.detail: 15 years · Standard Chartered, sole lender and lead arranger · Backed by IBRD first-loss and MIGA second-loss guarantees
register.note: West Africa’s first sustainability-linked sovereign loan, the World Bank says
register.text: A commercial loan whose interest rate steps down or up with the share of non-hydro renewables in installed power capacity by 2030 and with targets to limit forest loss and restore one million hectares of forest. The proceeds go to the general budget. It ties the cost of borrowing to cleaner power and standing forest.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 54 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy market street in Abidjan, Cote d Ivoire

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Cocoa and cashew smallholder farms in central Cote d Ivoire

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Tropical rainforest of Tai National Park, Cote d Ivoire

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: The Ebrie Lagoon at Abidjan with the city beyond

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: A hydropower dam on the Bandama River, Cote d Ivoire

items.name: Pouyou
items.text: An Ivorian company founded in 2021 that makes fortified infant cereals at Bingerville to fight child malnutrition, from raw materials bought from small local farmers.

items.name: CAFREX (Compagnie Africaine d’Expertise Agricole)
items.text: Produces and sells locally grown Ivorian rice and provides mechanised services to rice producers, selling to wholesalers, cooperatives and from its own outlet in Abidjan.

items.name: SODECI
items.text: The water distribution company of the Eranove group, which serves more than 2 million urban households.

items.name: ZECI
items.text: A joint venture that has sold solar home kits in Côte d’Ivoire since the end of 2016 on 36-month lease contracts prepaid monthly by mobile money, bringing electricity to more than 100,000 rural households.

items.name: Conceptos Plásticos
items.text: A Colombian social enterprise whose factory in Abidjan, built in 2019, turns plastic waste collected mostly by women into bricks for school classrooms, 262 of which have been built.

items.name: La Ruche Health
items.text: An Abidjan health start-up whose AI assistant Kiko, on WhatsApp, has answered more than 500,000 health questions, and which has arranged more than 5,000 paid teleconsultations with specialists, paid mostly by mobile money.

items.name: Yarani
items.text: A private vocational school in Abidjan, founded in 1990 by the association Education et Développement, that trains only women, in catering, hospitality and nurse aid.

coverage.gap_text: Of Ivorian children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2019.

guarantees.name: Education
